description: Ground-truth question set for the four-document demo corpus in bridge/corpus/. Every question names which document(s) the answer must come from, so a scoring run can tell 'retrieved the wrong document but the model covered anyway' apart from a genuine miss. Categories exist to stop a single easy majority (single-fact lookups) from flattering an aggregate score — see README.md in this directory for how to read a run.

categories.single_fact: One number or fact, stated once, in one document.
categories.multi_fact: Requires combining two or more facts from the same document.
categories.cross_document_distractor: Shares vocabulary with a document that is NOT the correct source — tests whether retrieval and generation both resist the lexical decoy.
categories.unanswerable: Not covered by any document in this corpus. The only correct answer is a refusal (confidence: none) — an invented answer is a failure regardless of how plausible it sounds.
categories.cross_document_synthesis: The full answer genuinely requires facts from two different documents.

questions.question: What is the maximum notional value allowed for a single order?
expected_key_facts: MAX_NOTIONAL_PER_ORDER_USD = 15_000_000.00

questions.question: How many years of ledger data must be retained?
questions.expected_answer: 7 years
expected_key_facts: LEDGER_RETENTION_YEARS = 7

questions.question: Who is authorized to re-arm the trading kill switch after it engages, and what does that require?
questions.expected_answer: Cryptographic authorization from two independent operators; a single desk head cannot do it alone.
expected_key_facts: Re-arming the kill switch requires cryptographic authorization from two independent operators.
A single desk head cannot reset the system alone.

questions.question: What crash-rate threshold triggers an automatic kill switch and rollback?
questions.expected_answer: Crash-free session rate below 99.5% over any rolling 4-hour window, or any single crash signature above 0.3% of sessions.
expected_key_facts: Crash-free session rate drops below 99.5% for the canary cohort over any rolling 4-hour window.
Any single crash signature accounts for more than 0.3% of all sessions on the build.
questions.notes: Three documents each describe their own 'automatic kill switch' with different trigger conditions (trading drawdown, deploy error rate, crash rate). This question's vocabulary ('kill switch', 'automatic') matches all three; only mobile_release_policy.md's numbers answer it.

questions.question: How many rejected requests in how many seconds triggers an automated response?
questions.expected_answer: More than 40 rejected orders inside 60 seconds.
expected_key_facts: More than 40 rejected orders occur inside 60 seconds.
questions.notes: platform_reliability_runbook.md has a similarly-shaped trigger ('25 pod crash-loops... inside 60 seconds') that is NOT the answer to this question.

questions.question: What P99 latency threshold pages the on-call engineer?
expected_key_facts: P99_LATENCY_PAGE_THRESHOLD_MS = 1800

questions.question: For a Severity 1 incident, who gets paged and in what order if nobody acknowledges?
questions.expected_answer: On-call primary immediately; secondary after 5 minutes unacknowledged; reliability lead after 10 minutes total unacknowledged.
expected_key_facts: Pages the on-call primary immediately via PagerDuty.
If unacknowledged within 5 minutes, escalation pages the secondary
if still unacknowledged after 10 minutes total, the reliability lead is paged directly.

questions.question: How many days of warning does an employee get before something is automatically revoked for being out of date?
questions.expected_answer: 3 days (enrollment grace period before internal app access is revoked for an out-of-date OS).
expected_key_facts: ENROLLMENT_GRACE_PERIOD_DAYS (3 days) of warnings before internal app access is automatically revoked
questions.notes: mobile_release_policy.md's STABLE_PROMOTION_DELAY_DAYS (10 days) is a different kind of delay on a different kind of automatic action; a model that pattern-matches on 'days before automatic X' alone can pick the wrong document.

questions.question: What is the minimum passcode length required for an enrolled device?
questions.expected_answer: 6 characters
expected_key_facts: PASSCODE_MIN_LENGTH = 6

questions.question: Can Restricted-tier data ever be cached on an employee-owned device?
questions.expected_answer: No — Restricted data must never be stored on an employee-owned device in any form, only viewed through a remote session with no local copy.
expected_key_facts: Restricted data must never be stored on an employee-owned device in any form, including screenshots, clipboard history, or offline caches.
Restricted data may only be viewed through a remote session that leaves no local copy.

questions.question: What is the data retention period measured in years mentioned in this corpus, and which system does it apply to?
questions.expected_answer: Ambiguous by design — there are at least three different year-denominated retention figures (ledger: 7 years; HR records: 7 years; email: 5 years) across two documents.
questions.notes: Deliberately underspecified. A good answer either asks which system, lists all matching figures with sources, or picks one AND cites which document/field it came from rather than presenting a single number as if it were the only one in the corpus. Scored manually, not by exact-match.

questions.question: How many days before a scheduled stable promotion does the soft code freeze begin?
questions.expected_answer: 5 days
expected_key_facts: A soft freeze begins 5 days before a scheduled stable promotion

questions.question: What happens if a device is not confirmed wiped within the escalation window after offboarding?
questions.expected_answer: It escalates to a full-device wipe request, which needs the device owner's manager to approve.
expected_key_facts: If the device does not check in and confirm the wipe within FULL_WIPE_ESCALATION_DAYS (14 days), the case escalates to a full-device wipe request
which requires the device owner's manager to approve

questions.question: What is the company's policy on remote work stipends?
questions.expected_answer: Not covered by this corpus.

questions.question: Which cloud provider hosts the settlement ledger's database?
questions.expected_answer: Not covered by this corpus.

questions.question: What is the escalation path if a Severity 3 incident is not resolved within 24 hours?
questions.expected_answer: Not covered — the runbook defines Severity 3 as no-page, but states no escalation path or time bound for it at all.
questions.notes: Adjacent-fact trap: the corpus discusses Severity 1/2 escalation timing extensively, which can tempt a model into extrapolating a Severity 3 timeline that was never stated.

questions.question: Both the trading system and the mobile release pipeline describe an automatic kill switch that can be resumed by different levels of approval — compare who can resume each one.
questions.expected_answer: Trading: requires cryptographic authorization from two independent operators (a single desk head cannot do it alone). Mobile release: the mobile lead alone can resume it, by attaching a root-cause note to the release ticket.
questions.notes: Tests whether retrieval pulls chunks from both documents for one query, and whether the model keeps the two approval paths distinct rather than merging them.

questions.question: What is the maximum universal APK size allowed?
questions.expected_answer: 200 MB
expected_key_facts: MAX_APK_SIZE_MB_UNIVERSAL = 200

questions.question: How long after discovering a lost device must it be reported?
questions.expected_answer: Within 2 hours of discovery.
expected_key_facts: A lost or stolen device enrolled in device management must be reported within 2 hours of discovery.

questions.question: What clock-skew anomaly between gateways is treated as a kill-switch trigger?
questions.expected_answer: An anomalous clock skew greater than 250 microseconds between gateways.
expected_key_facts: An anomalous clock skew greater than 250 microseconds is detected between gateways.
